title: House Democrats Probe Nvidia’s Role in U.S. Megaspeed Investigation
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

House Democrats are examining whether Nvidia influenced a U.S. Commerce Department investigation into suspected diversion of advanced chips to China. The inquiry centers on Nvidia’s contacts with officials investigating Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing company and Nvidia partner.

In a Nov. 19 letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Reps. Gregory Meeks of New York and Sydney Kamlager-Dove of California asked whether the department allowed Nvidia to interfere with export-control enforcement. The lawmakers requested answers and relevant documents by Dec. 1, Reuters reported after reviewing the letter. Meeks is the ranking Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

The Commerce and Justice departments said the federal investigation began in 2024 after Commerce identified suspicious activity while monitoring potential chip diversion. Investigators sought records from Nvidia in May 2025 on direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. The following month, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list, and U.S. and Singaporean officials conducted an on-site check and interviewed then-CEO Alice Huang. The Justice Department subsequently took the lead on the criminal investigation.

A Commerce official told Reuters that Nvidia contacted department employees directly in August 2025 and sought a meeting with one of them. According to the official, Nvidia told the employees that Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler had authorized the company to communicate with them.

Nvidia said it consults Commerce officials to answer questions, share information and seek guidance, and that it looks forward to engaging with Congress. Megaspeed said it complies with applicable laws, including U.S. export controls. A spokesperson for Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security said the bureau follows enforcement procedures and pursues chip smuggling aggressively.

The Nov. 19 letter follows a separate request from House Democrats for records from Cantor Fitzgerald. In that inquiry, lawmakers are examining whether the investment firm’s Nvidia holdings influenced Lutnick’s decisions on chip export restrictions.
